summary.headline: Ipca Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 14% to INR2,910 crores, with consolidated EBITDA margin up to 22.97% from 21.68%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew about 14% YoY to roughly INR2,910 crores from INR2,557 crores, and consolidated EBITDA margin expanded to about 22.97% from 21.68%, despite higher input, freight, shipping and energy costs. Standalone EBITDA margin improved to 26.6% from 25.46%. Domestic formulations grew about 14% to INR1,157 crores, with the Zerodol umbrella brand crossing INR1,500 crores annual sales. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 14-16% growth and 22-23% consolidated EBITDA margin, and said the UK business turned profitable after prior-year losses. Unichem's margin dipped on freight and air-shipment costs.

segments.name: Domestic formulations
segments.commentary: Grew about 14% to INR1,157 crores; market share 2.11% in MAT Sep 2026 (vs 2.09%), rank 16 per IQVIA. Chronic segment grew about 20% vs IPM about 17%; acute about 11%.

segments.name: Pain / Zerodol franchise
segments.commentary: Pain segment grew about 16% in Q2 to INR628 crores (from INR543 crores) and about 14% in H1. Zerodol rank improved to 8th from 11th; umbrella brand above INR1,500 crores, which management expects to grow similarly for 3-4 years.

segments.name: Export formulations (standalone)
segments.commentary: Grew 32% to INR653 crores. Europe generics up about 23%, Australia/NZ about 24%, US about 31%, Canada about 45%, South Africa about 46%.

segments.name: Institutional generics
segments.commentary: Grew about 45% in the quarter; H1 institutional sales about INR236 crores against full-year guidance of INR300 crores, which management now expects to exceed (INR325-340 crores).

segments.name: Unichem (US and Europe)
segments.commentary: Unichem US portfolio about USD38.5 million in the quarter; Ipca US portfolio about USD5.8 million. Freight rose about INR31 crores, with air share rising to about 25% from 5-6%. Brazil moved to profit after two loss-making quarters.

segments.name: UK subsidiary
segments.commentary: Returned to profit in FY27 after a loss of about GBP/USD 2.5 million in the prior year from old, sub-cost-priced products; market prices are recovering.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance of 14-16% (revised up from 12-13%) reiterated; management said it is not revising guidance.
FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin guidance of 22-23% reiterated.
Medium term: consolidated EBITDA margin to improve about 1-1.25% per year; standalone EBITDA to grow about 1.5%.
Domestic branded business guidance of 15-16% growth for India reiterated; H1 branded growth about 22%, with West Asia shipment delays causing about a 3% decline in one geography.
Institutional business full-year FY27 likely above INR300 crores (INR325-340 crores), but management does not expect significant growth and it may decline next year.
Unichem EBITDA margin may stay at 11-13% if freight and energy costs remain high; Unichem gross margin around 58% with 1-2% variation expected.
Interest cost expected to decline in H2 as the remaining rupee term loan (about INR155 crores) is reduced to about INR70-75 crores by year-end.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity, utilisation or commissioning timelines were discussed on the call.
Medium-term consolidated EBITDA margin expected to improve about 1-1.25% per year; standalone EBITDA to grow about 1.5%, per management (no capex figures given).
Unichem EBITDA margin about 11.3% in Q2; may stay at 11-13% if freight and energy costs remain high (no capacity data given).
demand_pricing: Zerodol volume growth about 8-9% and price growth about 4-4.5% within the 14-16% pain segment growth.
Input, logistics, shipping and energy costs rose significantly in the quarter.
Acute segment growth lagged the chronic segment; antimalarials, antibacterials and cough and cold are declining or growing very slowly.
Unichem freight costs up about INR31 crores QoQ; other expenses rose from INR142 crores to INR189 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Zerodol franchise growth, volume/price split, and headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Pain segment grew 16% in Q2 to INR628 crores; volume about 8-9%, price about 4-4.5%. Management expects similar growth for 3-4 years from the INR1,500 crore umbrella brand.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance being revised, and what is medium-term margin expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance stands at 14-16% growth and 22-23% consolidated EBITDA margin. Consolidated EBITDA margin is expected to improve about 1-1.25% per year; standalone EBITDA to grow about 1.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove Unichem's gross margin uptick, and is it sustainable? What are Unichem's US growth figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin was held back by freight and a rise in air shipments to about 25% of volume, costing about INR30 crores. Gross margin of about 58% is sustainable within 1-2%. Unichem US portfolio was USD38.5 million; Ipca US about USD5.8 million, with overall US portfolio growth about 9% in dollars.

qa_highlights.question: Will institutional sales be lumpy, and is the INR300 crore guidance maintained?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR25 crores of shipments slipped from last year into Q1. FY27 likely to exceed INR300 crores (INR325-340 crores) but growth will not be significant and may decline next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is branded business on track for 15% growth, and will H2 be soft?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 branded growth about 22%, with West Asia shipment delays causing about a 3% decline in one geography. Management maintains 15-16% India branded growth guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is interest cost still high, and where does it go in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Foreign currency debt was repaid last year, so Q2 interest did not rise. Only about INR155 crores of rupee term loan remains, to be cut to about INR70-75 crores by year-end; interest cost should decline in H2. Company holds about INR700 crores of cash.

qa_highlights.question: How are European, UK and subsidiary businesses performing?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe generics up about 23%, Australia/NZ about 24%. UK returned to profit after prior-year losses as market prices recover. All subsidiaries are profitable except Pisgah, which is expected to improve next fiscal year on API order positions.

risks_watch: Freight, air-shipment, energy and input cost inflation could keep Unichem EBITDA margin at 11-13%.
Institutional business is lumpy and not expected to grow significantly; it may decline next year.
Acute segment and antibacterial/antimalarial portfolios are weak; West Asia shipment delays affected one branded geography.
Pisgah (US API subsidiary) remains loss-making and is not expected to improve until next fiscal year.
Brazil profitability for Unichem is recent (first profit after two loss quarters) and needs to hold.
summary.management_tone: Confident on domestic and export growth and on guidance, which was reiterated without change. Cautious on Unichem margins and on institutional business, which management described as conservative and lumpy. Answers on Pisgah and the UK were brief.
key_quotes: So we have absolutely no concern on that.
We are not revising the guidelines.
So practically, we are debt-free company because we are getting almost around INR700 crores cash in books and debt are hardly any.
